Rural

ROOR-uhl · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Rural is relating to the countryside, not a city or town.

My grandparents live in a rural area where cornfields stretch for miles.

Worked Example

The rural school has only two classrooms, but every student knows everyone's name.

A tiny school with farms all around it tells you it is out in the countryside. Places in the countryside are rural.

How Rural Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

country

country: in or like the countryside

farming

farming: full of farms and fields

Antonyms

urban

urban: relating to cities

city

city: in a busy town area

How Strong Is It? — Suburban → Remote → rural

Suburban vs. rural

Suburban vs. rural: Suburban is in between: a suburban street has houses close together just outside a city.

Remote vs. rural

Remote vs. rural: Remote is stronger: a remote cabin is far from any town at all, even deeper in the countryside than a rural farm.

Build the Word

The pieces

root — rur

root — rur: the countryside (Latin (rus, ruris))

suffix — al

suffix — al: characteristic of, relating to (Latin)

Put it together

Put it together: Rur- means the countryside in Latin, so rural describes places out in the country.

Use the root in a new word: countryside

Use the root in a new word: countryside: The train ride through the countryside was full of barns and hay bales. (Fun fact: the Latin root of rural is very old and rare - rural is almost the only everyday English word that still uses it.)
